concern: Four generated-artifact checks inside the required gate grade a committed artifact against a rebuild from the mutable working tree, so uncommitted work anywhere in the tree makes them report the artifact stale when it is correct.

claims_under_test: docs/surface.html reported stale under verify while the committed bytes were correct
the check's referent is the working tree rather than committed state

observer_relation.basis: Found while chasing a finding another session reported and left unchased. This session did not build any of the checks named here and is not repairing them.

shared_tree_conditions.mitigation: this finding is ABOUT the shared tree, so it was measured in it deliberately. The digest readings were repeated six times to separate nondeterminism from contention.

checks.result: PASS standalone, three times, on the committed bytes
FAIL: repository hygiene, orientation snapshot, diagram provenance, Node Interface projection, documentation reader, operation surface page, repository tooling tests

reproduced.claim: the surface check's referent is a live rebuild, not a frozen one
reproduced.finding: command_check compares PAGE.read_text() against build(); build() calls surface(), which calls rebuild() to re-derive the interface from current sources. The docstring says so plainly: 'Rebuild the canonical interface; the checked projection is never an input.' The comparison is therefore committed bytes against a working-tree derivation, and any session writing a source file during the run moves one side of it.

reproduced.claim: the derivation is deterministic, so the flap is contention and not nondeterminism
reproduced.method: computed input_state_digest six times in succession on the shared tree
reproduced.finding: six identical digests, zero defects each time. The derivation is stable when nothing writes. That matters because it rules out the easy explanation: the check is not flaky in itself, it is exact about an input that other participants are changing underneath it.

reproduced.claim: a sibling check was already repaired for exactly this hazard
reproduced.method: read scripts/sov_snapshot.py and grepped all five generated-artifact checks for git or HEAD references
reproduced.finding: sov_snapshot.py states it directly: 'Before the ruling every count globbed the tree, and one [failed] everyone on the branch against an unmoved HEAD.' It now routes every reach through sovsnapshot/committed.py. It is the only one of the five that does. sov_surface.py, sov_docs.py, sov_diagrams.py and sov_interface.py carry zero git or HEAD references between them.

reproduced.claim: this is the mechanism behind the red shared tree reported earlier tonight
reproduced.method: compared the failing check list from a full verify run against the four working-tree readers
reproduced.finding: the run failed on diagram provenance, Node Interface projection, documentation reader and operation surface page - which is exactly the set of checks that rebuild from the working tree - plus orientation snapshot and hygiene. The earlier reading attributed the red tree to collisions between sessions. The more precise mechanism is that these checks grade a committed artifact against uncommitted state, so any session's unstaged work makes them report stale.

residuals.finding: This is a false failure in a required check. The Gate ruleset requires repository (3.11) and repository (3.12), which run verify.py, which runs these checks. On CI the tree is clean so the failure does not appear there; it appears on any working tree with uncommitted work, which is every local landing path. sov_land.py runs verify locally before the gate, so this refuses local landings on the strength of other people's unstaged edits.

No decisions/ record was found stating the committed-state ruling; sov_snapshot.py refers to it as 'the ruling' and the merge commit names it. If the principle is settled, applying it to the remaining four checks is ordinary work rather than a new decision. If it is not, this is the second instance and the case for settling it.

Not every one of the four should necessarily move to committed state. A check that exists to tell an author 'you edited a source and did not re-render' is correct to read the working tree; that is its job. The distinction worth drawing is between a check that grades an artifact against its declared sources and one that tells an author to re-run a builder. Repairing this without drawing that line would trade a false failure for a missed one.

not_examined: whether each of the four checks should read committed state, or only the ones that grade rather than remind
standing_supported: none. This is a defect report, not a witness of any change. It settles nothing and proposes no transition. It is recorded because it is the mechanism behind a reading this session gave Bdo earlier in less precise terms.
judgement_items: Four checks in the required gate grade committed artifacts against a working-tree rebuild while a fifth was repaired to read committed state. Whether the remaining four follow it is a verification domain question with an existing precedent, not obviously an owner one - but the precedent is referred to as a ruling and no decision record for it was found.
